page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.large is an entry-tier virtual instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, it features simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache.

Benchmark measurements position the instance within the lower tier across standardized tests. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves 1093.88 in single-core performance (bottom 25%) and 1458.47 in multi-core throughput (bottom 10%). Geekbench testing mirrors this with scores of 919.0 for single-core and 1093.0 for multi-core. Memory subsystem performance registers uncached read bandwidth at 9.92 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 9.22 GB/sec for large 256 MB blocks, ranking in the bottom 10%. Application benchmarks show 1.47 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 1.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, necessitating reliance on networked block storage for persistent volumes. Baseline network interface bandwidth is specified at 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because hardware resources are constrained to a single physical core and 4.0 GB of RAM, throughput under parallel execution is limited by thread contention on the single execution engine.

Given its compact footprint and low compute density, the instance provides cost efficiency for non-demanding services that do not require high computational headroom or heavy local disk IOPS. Appropriate operational fits include lightweight microservices, low-traffic web servers, testing environments, network proxies, and ancillary support services with modest memory and processing demands.

The instance omits local disk storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reflect entry-level performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1093.88 and multi-core reaching 1458.47, placing compute and memory metrics largely in the lower quartile.
